result.title: Size-Matched Nulls Reveal What Block Ablation Measures in MambaVision
result.summary: Hybrid vision backbones interleave Mamba state-space mixers with self-attention, and a block's role is usually probed by removing it and measuring the damage. We test what that measurement means in MambaVision. On all 50,000 ImageNet validation images and three model sizes, every block ablation is paired with a size-matched null, the same perturbation with its channels shuffled or their signs flipped. In top-1 accuracy and in true-class rank, real and null damage are nearly indistinguishable in absolute terms: pooled over the blocks of MambaVision-T, the content effect lies within [-0.044,+0.016] percentage points (90% interval). Two attention-only controls show that the test detects content, with real ablations worse than their nulls by up to 4.2 points in DeiT-Small and 1.0 point in Swin-T. Part of MambaVision's near-equivalence reflects how little damage its blocks do (0.11--0.34 points on average, against 1.7 and 2.1). Scaled by damage, its content share is comparable to Swin-T's in accuracy, lower in rank, and far below DeiT-Small's: single-block damage in MambaVision is small and mostly positional. Ablation also hides what blocks carry together: removing all blocks of one type compounds damage to 3.7--8.4 times the sum of single effects, far more than size-matched nulls, including nulls that keep the alignment between the blocks' perturbations; for adjacent pairs, aligned nulls reproduce most of it. Freezing input-dependent selection in all Mamba mixers shows that it accounts for 20--32% of the Mamba contribution, mainly through the B and C projections. We turn these results into a protocol for causal attribution in hybrid networks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 MambaVision 上用尺寸匹配的零对照（通道打乱或符号翻转）配对每个块消融，在 ImageNet 全验证集和三个模型尺寸上发现真实与零消融造成的损伤几乎无法区分，并据此提出混合网络的因果归因协议。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「对齐零假设」与成对块复合效应设计，可供核查 LVR 中消融式贡献分配是否混入了扰动规模、位置等混淆，为评价 latent 组件的因果作用提供方法线索。
